ASV diagnostics differ from E-values~\cite{vanderweele_ding2017} in three respects (Table~\ref{tab:sensitivity_comparison}, Appendix):

\paragraph{Measurement error in causal inference.}
The foundations are established in \citet{carroll2006}, \citet{gustafson2004}, \citet{buonaccorsi2010}, and \citet{bound2001measurement}, with starred-node DAGs formalized by \citet{hernan_cole2009} and DAG-based correction theory developed by \citet{kuroki_pearl2014}. For binary variables, non-differential misclassification biases toward the null~\cite{brenner1993, ogburn_vanderweele2012}, with \citet{neuhaus1999} quantifying the attenuation and efficiency loss in binary regression under known misclassification rates; but this fails for polytomous exposures~\cite{dosemeci1990, jurek2005, veirod_laake2001}. \citet{edwards_lessler_naimi2021} showed dependent misclassification can bias in either direction, \citet{imai_yamamoto2010} provide nonparametric identification under differential measurement error, \citet{nguimkeu_denteh_tchernis2019} address endogenous treatment misreporting, and \citet{shu_yi2019a, shu_yi2019b} develop weighted estimators that jointly handle mismeasured covariates and misclassified outcomes under IPW---a concern that also drives mediation analyses with mismeasured mediators~\cite{imai_keele_tingley2010, valeri_vanderweele2013, valeri_vanderweele2014}. \citet{schennach2020mismeasured} addresses general nonclassical measurement error in regression; \citet{miles2024measurement} construct instrumental variables for measurement-error-robust estimation; \citet{wei2025multiply} develop multiply robust estimators under misclassified treatment. All analyze a single DAG topology; ours is the first to characterize how the \emph{same} confusion matrix produces qualitatively different bias across seven topologies.

\paragraph{Measurement error in causal inference.}
Foundations appear in \citet{carroll2006, gustafson2004, buonaccorsi2010, bound2001measurement}, with DAG-based formalization by \citet{hernan_cole2009} and \citet{kuroki_pearl2014}. For binary variables, non-differential misclassification biases toward the null~\cite{brenner1993, ogburn_vanderweele2012}, but this fails for polytomous exposures~\cite{dosemeci1990, jurek2005, veirod_laake2001}. Extensions address differential measurement error~\cite{edwards_lessler_naimi2021, imai_yamamoto2010}, endogenous misreporting~\cite{nguimkeu_denteh_tchernis2019}, mismeasured covariates under IPW~\cite{shu_yi2019a, shu_yi2019b}, mediation with mismeasured mediators~\cite{valeri_vanderweele2013}, nonclassical error~\cite{schennach2020mismeasured}, and multiply robust estimation~\cite{wei2025multiply}. All analyze a single DAG topology; ours characterizes how the \emph{same} confusion matrix produces qualitatively different bias across seven topologies.

\paragraph{Sensitivity analysis and correction methods.}
Our ASV framework draws on the sensitivity analysis without assumptions of \citet{ding_vanderweele2016}, E-values~\cite{vanderweele_ding2017, mathur2018}, the robustness value of \citet{cinelli2020making}, and the mediation sensitivity analysis of \citet{imai_keele_yamamoto2010}, and text-based causal inference methods~\cite{pryzant_etal2021}, but parametrises annotation error severity rather than omitted variable strength or sequential ignorability violations. The quantitative bias analysis framework of \citet{lash2009} provides a complementary epidemiologic perspective, and \citet{mahajan2006} establishes identification of regression models with misclassified regressors via instrumental variables. The unified measurement-error and missing-data framework of \citet{blackwell_honaker_king2017} similarly motivates treating annotation noise as a first-class object of inference. For correction, PPI++~\cite{angelopoulos2023} and DSL~\cite{egami_hinck_stewart_wei2023} are topology-agnostic; \citet{zrnic_candes2024} extend PPI to gold-free settings, \citet{demirel2024prediction} generalize prediction-powered inference to causal parameters across populations, and \citet{cadei2025} adapt it to treatment-effect targets via a deconfounded risk objective, and \citet{gligoric2025} leverage LLM confidence scores. Our contribution reveals that this agnosticism is costly: correction effectiveness is itself topology-dependent, with matrix-based methods provably ineffective for four topologies. Bayesian measurement error models~\cite{richardson1993bayesian, gustafson2004} and EM imputation offer alternatives that bypass FWL invariance.

The quantitative bias analysis framework of \citet{lash2009} provides a complementary epidemiologic perspective, and \citet{mahajan2006} establishes identification of regression models with misclassified regressors via instrumental variables. The unified measurement-error and missing-data framework of \citet{blackwell_honaker_king2017} similarly motivates treating annotation noise as a first-class object of inference. Our contribution reveals that this agnosticism is costly: correction effectiveness is itself topology-dependent, with matrix-based methods provably ineffective for four topologies.
